newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy inflation shows impact of policy - official.
newsitem.headline: Italy inflation shows impact of policy - official.

text.p: Italian inflation figures for August were further evidence government economic policy, which includes action to cut utility prices as a means of controlling inflation while also protecting salaries, was paying off, a senior Treasury Ministry official said.

"We are increasingly convinced that we have a lowering of structural inflation which is due to a series of factors. The economic slowdown throughout Europe is not one of them," the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said.
The annual rate fell in August to 3.4 percent, the lowest for 27 years. The figure followed a 3.6 percent rise in the consumer price index in July and was the seventh successive drop.
The government has set an average annual inflation target of 2.5 percent for 1997.
